groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Last summer, Maya decided to embark on a journey that would forever broaden her perspective on life. She had always been curious about places far from her hometown, and this trip promised experiences that would __(16: deepen)__ her understanding of different cultures.
On the first day, she visited a small village nestled among rolling hills. The locals welcomed her with radiant smiles. Maya felt a sense of __(17: fascination)__ as she explored the winding streets, each corner revealing a new surprise.
In the evenings, she would sit by the river, watching the sunset that seemed to __(18: illuminate)__ the sky with brilliant shades of orange and pink. These moments reminded her that life was not just about achievements, but also about the beauty that surrounded her.
One afternoon, while hiking a steep trail, Maya encountered an elderly man who was __(19: frail)__ yet radiated a quiet wisdom. He shared inspirational stories of his youth, and Maya listened intently, knowing that these narratives would __(20: enlighten)__ her in ways books never could. By the end of the trip, Maya felt transformed.
Adapted from The Unexpected Journey

Study the poster (Text 1) and the extract from an article (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below shows a poster.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
Wearing the right shoes is important for every runner, whether they are experienced athletes or beginners. Good running shoes do more than keep the feet comfortable. They play a key role in helping runners perform well and in preventing injuries.
Firstly, proper running shoes provide strong support and sufficient cushioning. When a runner's feet hit the ground, the shoes help to absorb the impact. This reduces pressure on the feet, ankles and knees, making running safer. It also lowers the risk of common injuries such as sprains, muscle strain and joint pain.
In addition, running shoes are designed to help the body move correctly. They improve balance and support smoother, more controlled movements while running. With better stability and posture, runners can run more efficiently and for longer periods without discomfort.
In conclusion, choosing the right pair of running shoes may seem like a simple decision, but it is an important one. The right shoes help runners enjoy their runs, improve their performance and protect their bodies from injury.

images.alt: Poster with a picture of a running shoe that has a wing at the heel. Text: Join us for the sales launch of the FALCON! DON'T RUN, FLY! Exclusively for Sports House members at the Vista City Outlet. 12 December at 10 a.m. $129.90 Members' Price. Only 100 pairs! No reservations for customers or online purchases. Six feature boxes: A) Lightweight: Makes running easier and faster. B) Cushioned Comfort: Keeps your feet free from blisters. C) Grippy Soles: Helps you stay steady on any surface. D) Visibility: Reflective materials keep you visible in low light. E) Durability: Built to last through many kilometres. F) Support: Provides stability for injury-free running. At the bottom: Visit www.sportshouse.sg for more information.

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
[[table1]]

Hiccups are sudden, repeated sounds that happen when your body makes a small "jump" inside your chest. They occur __(26)__ the diaphragm, a muscle under the lungs __(27)__ helps you breathe, suddenly contracts. This quick movement makes you breathe __(28)__ air very fast. At the same time, the gap between your vocal cords snaps shut, causing __(29)__ familiar "hic" sound.
There are __(30)__ reasons why hiccups occur. You might eat or drink too quickly, swallow too much air or even laugh too hard. Sometimes, feeling nervous or excited can also make you get hiccups. In most cases, hiccups last only a few minutes and stop on __(31)__ own.
To get rid __(32)__ hiccups, people often try holding their breath, drinking water slowly or breathing into a paper bag. __(33)__ methods help the diaphragm relax so that your breathing goes back __(34)__ normal. Hiccups are harmless, __(35)__ they can be annoying. The sounds are a normal part of how our bodies work.

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

Last Saturday, my family gathered at a bustling seafood restaurant. It was a special __(36: occassion)__ as it was Grandma's eightieth birthday. My cousin, Sarah, who cared deeply about her __(37: appearence)__, arrived wearing a stunning silk dress that shimmered under the chandeliers. However, she soon felt __(38: embrassed)__ and her confidence vanished when she realised she had accidentally __(39: wore)__ one black sandal and one navy blue slipper __(40: on)__ her frantic rush to leave home. Everyone at the table chuckled __(41: soft)__ at the sight, but Grandma gave her a warm, __(42: comfort)__ hug to make her feel better.
During the lively party, Grandma __(43: receives)__ many wonderful gifts from her grandchildren, ranging from handmade cards to __(44: elegeant)__ jewellery. My brother gave her a brand-new tablet, explaining that it would be much more __(45: convinient)__ for her to video call us whenever she missed hearing our voices or seeing our faces. Grandma smiled brightly, her eyes twinkling with joy as she thanked us all for such a memorable day.

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

Being a responsible member of the school community means more than just attending classes on time. It involves showing courtesy to teachers, classmates, and staff __(46)__ simple greetings, such as saying "please" and "thank you". These polite behaviours create a positive and friendly environment where __(47)__ feels valued.
Respecting school rules is another important part of being responsible. Rules are designed to __(48)__ safety, fairness, and order for all. For instance, __(49)__ patiently for one's turn, keeping noise levels low in the library, and following instructions in the classroom are ways to demonstrate self-discipline and __(50)__ for others.
Think about how your actions __(51)__ possibly affect other people. Helping a classmate who has dropped her books, offering to share materials, or including quieter students in group __(52)__ are all examples of thoughtfulness and kindness.
A responsible student also takes care of both __(53)__ and shared resources. This includes returning borrowed books on time, keeping the canteen clean, and using school property __(54)__ care. Students must not forget to appreciate the efforts of those who maintain the school grounds.
Communication and cooperation are equally important. Listening attentively, speaking politely, and working well in teams help to strengthen existing bonds __(55)__ maintain good relationships with others. Handling disagreements __(56)__ they arise shows emotional maturity.
What about diligence? Is a diligent student a responsible one? Most certainly! Completing assignments on time, and asking questions when you are in __(57)__ about a difficult concept taught in class reflect a commitment to learning.
Finally, responsible students promote a positive school culture by participating in community activities, __(58)__ kind towards newcomers, and helping others in need. These actions will help make the school environment safe and conducive for all. By demonstrating positive __(59)__ such as graciousness and gratitude each day, students __(60)__ to a better school experience for both their peers and teachers. That way, everyone within the school community can flourish and find joy in shared everyday experiences.
Adapted from Social Responsibility in School

Refer to the passage below when you answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** Brian's eyes snapped open. He was unbelievably, viciously thirsty. His mouth was dry and tasted foul and sticky. His lips were cracked and seemed as if they were bleeding. His skin was all withered up. He knew the thirst and felt the burn on his face. It was mid-afternoon. The sun had come over him and cooked him while he slept. His face felt like it was on fire. **It** was going to blister and peel.
**2** He stood, using the tree to pull himself up because there was still some pain and much stiffness and looked down towards the lake. It was water but he did not know if he could drink it. He felt the idea of drinking water from a lake was awful, but the lake was blue, looked clean and his mouth and throat raged with thirst. Would there be another water source he could drink from? Moreover, he had swallowed a lot of the water while he was swimming out of the plane and getting to shore.
**3** Brian felt helpless in a situation consisting of a plane wreck, a badly bruised forehead, an aching body and a thirst that tore at him until he could not think. He took small steps down the bank to the lake. Along the edge, there were thick prickly grasses in the way and the water looked a little murky. He scowled in disgust at the small bugs swimming in the water and was glad to see a log extending about ten metres out into the lake, with sturdy branches sticking up, almost like strong handles.
**4** He balanced on the log, holding himself up with the limbs, and teetered out past the weeds and muddy water. When he was out where the water was clear and he could see no bugs swimming, he kneeled on the log to drink. He thought he would just try a sip, still pondering over the lake water. However, when he brought a cupped hand to his mouth and felt the cold lake water trickle past his cracked lips and over his tongue, he could not stop.
**5** He had never, not even on long bicycle trips in the summer, been this thirsty. He stooped and put his mouth to the lake and drank and drank, pulling it deep and swallowing great gulps of it. He drank until his stomach was swollen, until he nearly fell off the log with **it**, then he got up and staggered his way back to the bank where he was immediately sick and threw up most of the water.
**6** However, his thirst was gone by then and the water seemed to reduce the pain in his head as well, although the sunburn still felt hot on his face. He pulled himself once more up the bank to the tall tree without branches and sat again with his back against **it**. It was hot now. The sun was high and he sat in the shade of the tree in relative comfort, but there were things he knew he had to do.
Adapted from "Hatchet" by Gary Paulsen

questions.stem:
Part 1: Situational Writing (14 marks)
The pictures below show Vincent, Siti and Meera having a conversation. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
(The next page of the question booklet, which prints the task and the points to include, is missing from the scan. From the conversation, the task is: imagine you are Vincent and write an email to your teacher, Miss Tan, to propose the class community service project.)

images.alt: Two comic panels set in a library, dated 17 August 2026, 11.45 a.m. Panel 1. Vincent: As part of our community service, let's fold 1,000 paper cranes to bring joy to the patients at Rosewood Hospital! Siti: Great idea, Vincent! We can call it 'Project Paper Crane' or 'Cranes for Smiles'! Meera: Siti, let's use your second suggestion. We'll definitely need coloured paper. We won't need glue, but we will need some nylon string to hang the paper cranes. Panel 2. Vincent: Alright, I'll email Miss Tan to propose this as our class community service project and tell her we need the materials by 15 October. Siti: No, Vincent. We must get the materials by 8 October so that we'll have enough time to fold the cranes. What do you think, Meera? Meera: Right, Siti! Vincent, you should also explain why our class is doing this as our community service project and the value it teaches us.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to propose a class community service project and ask for the materials. Audience: Miss Tan, your teacher, so the tone is polite and respectful. Context: you are Vincent, writing after the conversation on 17 August 2026.
Content point: what the project is. The class will fold 1,000 paper cranes to bring joy to the patients at Rosewood Hospital.
Content point: the name of the project. Meera chose Siti's **second** suggestion, so it is 'Cranes for Smiles', not 'Project Paper Crane'.
Content point: the materials needed. Coloured paper and nylon string (to hang the cranes). Do not ask for glue.
Content point: when the materials are needed. By 8 October, not 15 October; Siti corrected Vincent so that there is enough time to fold the cranes.

Content point: why the class is doing this and the value it teaches. The conversation does not give these, so supply sensible ones of your own, for example to cheer up patients who are unwell, and to learn compassion or care for others.
Format: an email with a greeting (Dear Miss Tan), short clear paragraphs, a polite closing line and your name (Vincent) at the end.
Language: full sentences, correct tenses, no chat abbreviations. Do not copy the speech bubbles word for word; change 'we' and 'let's' to fit an email to a teacher.

review.solvedAnswer: Checklist written from the conversation in the pictures.
review.note: Page 3 of 4 of the Paper 1 booklet (the task box with the exact wording and the list of points to include) is not in the PDF. The task and the content points in the checklist are inferred from the speech bubbles, so the exact wording and number of required points cannot be confirmed.

questions.stem:
Part 2: Continuous Writing (36 marks)
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **making a difference**.
The pictures are provided to help you think about the topic.
Your composition should be based on one or more of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
• Why was the act needed?
• What changed after the act?
You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures in a column. Picture 1: a silhouette of a younger person supporting an elderly person who walks with a stick. Picture 2: an open, empty cardboard box. Picture 3: a smiling cat sitting with a bandage wrapped around one front leg.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Understand the topic: 'making a difference' means doing something that changes a person's (or an animal's) situation for the better. The act can be small, but the story must show clearly what was different afterwards.
Picture 1 (helping an elderly person): you or a character could help an elderly neighbour who struggles to walk, shop or cross the road, and that help changes how lonely or unsafe the person feels.
Picture 2 (an empty box): the box could be filled, for example a donation drive of food, books or toys for a family or a home in need; or it could be a box in which something was found or delivered.
Picture 3 (a cat with a bandaged leg): a character could rescue an injured stray, take it to a vet and nurse it back to health.
Use at least one picture and make it important to the story, not just mentioned in passing.

Answer both guiding points. Why was the act needed? Show the problem first (what the person or animal was going through). What changed after the act? Show the result for the one helped and also for the one who helped.
Story arc: opening that sets the scene, the problem noticed, a decision to act (include a moment of hesitation or difficulty), the act itself in detail as the climax, then the outcome.
Ending: return to the topic. Reflect on how one act made a difference and what the main character learnt, so that the last paragraph links back to 'making a difference'.
Language: show feelings through actions and speech, vary your sentence openings, keep to the past tense, and write well over 150 words.

review.solvedAnswer: Planning checklist written for the topic.

questions.stem: "Father's eaten his lunch, __________?" Mary asked.

explanation: Rule: a question tag repeats the helping verb of the statement, and a positive statement takes a negative tag.
'Father's eaten' is short for 'Father **has** eaten', because 'eaten' is a past participle and it follows 'has', not 'is'.
The helping verb is 'has', so the tag is 'hasn't he'. 'isn't he' is the trap: 's can be 'is' or 'has', and here it is 'has'.
The answer is option (2), hasn't he.

review.note: The apostrophe in "Father's" has dropped out of the scan (it reads "Father s"); it is restored in the stem.

questions.stem: Rani is well-known __________ her expertise in growing orchids.

explanation: Some adjectives always go with a fixed preposition. We say a person is 'well-known **for**' or 'famous **for**' the thing that makes them known.
Rani's expertise in growing orchids is the reason people know her, so the word is 'for'.
'well-known by' would be followed by the people who know her (well-known by gardeners), not by the reason.
The answer is option (2), for.

questions.stem: "Won't Alice be excited when she __________ that she's representing the class for the speech competition?" Ben asked.

explanation: Rule: after time words such as 'when', 'after' and 'as soon as', use the simple present tense to talk about the future. Do not use 'will' in that part of the sentence.
'Won't Alice be excited' is about the future (will not), so the 'when' part takes the simple present: 'when she hears'.
'heard' is past tense, but Alice has not been told yet. 'has heard' is possible in some sentences, but here the excitement happens at the moment she hears, so the simple present fits best.
The answer is option (1), hears.

questions.stem: Mother objected to __________ the bag for Sarah as it was too expensive.

explanation: In 'object to', the word 'to' is a preposition, not part of a to-infinitive.
Rule: a verb that comes after a preposition takes the -ing form (a gerund): object to buying, look forward to seeing.
'buy' is the trap because 'to buy' looks right, but 'objected to buy' is wrong. 'having bought' would mean the bag was already bought, which does not fit an objection.
The answer is option (2), buying.

questions.stem: Tina made __________ progress in her studies because she had been revising diligently.

explanation: 'progress' is an uncountable noun (we cannot say 'two progresses'), so 'few' and 'many', which go with countable nouns, are out.
That leaves 'little' and 'much'. 'little progress' means hardly any; 'much progress' means a lot.
The reason given is that she 'had been revising diligently'. Hard work leads to a lot of progress, so 'much' fits the meaning.
The answer is option (3), much.

questions.stem: All the information about the upcoming school workshops __________ to the students last week.

explanation: Tense: 'last week' shows the past, so 'is given' and 'are given' are out.
Agreement: find the real subject. It is 'information', not 'workshops', which only sits in the phrase 'about the upcoming school workshops'.
'information' is uncountable and always takes a singular verb, even with 'all the' in front. So the verb is 'was given', not 'were given'.
The answer is option (3), was given.

questions.stem: The commitment displayed by the students __________ the reason why they did well in the project.

explanation: Agreement: the subject is 'The commitment' (singular). 'displayed by the students' only describes it, so do not let the plural 'students' trick you. 'are' and 'were' are out.
Tense: the rest of the sentence is in the past ('they **did** well in the project'), so the verb should be past too.
Singular and past gives 'was'. 'is' is tempting, but the project is over and the sentence is told in the past.
The answer is option (3), was.

questions.stem: The young boy helped the old lady __________ the busy road.

explanation: Rule: after help + a person, use the base form of the verb (with or without 'to'): helped her cross, helped her to cross.
The verb 'helped' already carries the past tense, so the second verb does not change: it stays 'cross'.
'crossed' is the trap because the sentence is in the past, but only the main verb 'helped' shows the tense.
The answer is option (1), cross.

questions.stem: If John __________ early last night, he would not have missed his school bus this morning.

explanation: This is a conditional about something in the past that did not happen: John did not sleep early, and he did miss the bus.
Rule (third conditional): If + had + past participle, ... would have + past participle. The second half has 'would not have missed', so the 'if' half needs 'had slept'.
'had been sleeping' describes an action in progress, not the completed act of going to sleep early. 'sleeps' and 'has slept' are present forms and do not match 'last night'.
The answer is option (3), had slept.

questions.stem: __________ his injury, the participant was unable to complete the race.

explanation: Work out how the two ideas are linked. The injury is the **cause**; being unable to finish is the **result**. We need a connector that shows a reason.
'Due to' means 'because of' and is followed by a noun phrase ('his injury').

'Despite' and 'Regardless of' show contrast: they would fit if he had finished the race even though he was hurt. 'Although' must be followed by a clause with a verb (Although he was injured), not just a noun phrase.
The answer is option (1), Due to.

questions.stem: The children were thrilled at the idea of going for a class learning journey. They felt __________ the entire day.

explanation: Clue: 'thrilled' in the first sentence. The second sentence repeats the same feeling, so we need a word for very happy and excited.
'exhilarated' means extremely happy and full of excitement.
'daunted' and 'apprehensive' both mean worried or afraid, which is the opposite. 'moved' means touched with emotion, such as by a sad story.
The answer is option (3), exhilarated.

questions.stem: To prevent people from getting too close to the turtle's nest on the beach, the Nature Lovers' Society __________ the area.

explanation: Clue: the aim is 'to prevent people from getting too close'. We need a phrasal verb meaning to block off a place so that people cannot enter.
'cordon off' means to put a rope, tape or barrier around an area to keep people out.

'fend off' means to defend yourself against an attack. 'round off' means to finish something nicely or to round a number. 'mark off' only shows a boundary; it does not carry the idea of keeping people out as strongly.
The answer is option (4), cordoned off.

questions.stem: The top student of the school __________ her success to her parents and teachers who had nurtured her in the formative years of her life.

explanation: Look at the pattern: ___ her success **to** her parents and teachers. The word must fit 'something to somebody' and mean 'said it was because of'.
'attribute something to someone' means to say that someone is the cause of it. She said her success was thanks to her parents and teachers.

'acknowledged' is tempting because it is about giving credit, but we acknowledge a person or a fact (she acknowledged her teachers' help); it does not take 'her success to'. 'associated' goes with 'with', and 'assigned' means gave out a task.
The answer is option (2), attributed.

questions.stem: The fight between Peter and Ming was __________ only because their teacher intervened.

explanation: Clue: 'only because their teacher intervened' (stepped in). The teacher stopped the fight from happening.
'averted' means prevented something bad from happening.
The other words look alike but mean different things: 'inverted' is turned upside down, 'diverted' is sent in another direction (diverted traffic), and 'reverted' is went back to an earlier state.
The answer is option (1), averted.

questions.stem: Due to time constraints, the debate team members ensured that their argument was brief and to the point. They were very __________.

explanation: Clue: 'brief and to the point'. We need the word that means saying what is needed in few words.
'concise' means short and clear, with no unnecessary words.
'precise' and 'accurate' mean exact and correct, and 'specific' means detailed and clear about one thing. A speech can be precise and still be long, so they do not match 'brief'.
The answer is option (3), concise.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++deepen++.

explanation: To 'deepen' her understanding is to make an understanding she already has stronger and fuller.
'enhance' means to improve something or make it greater, which matches.

'create' means to make something new, but she already has some understanding. 'foster' and 'cultivate' mean to help something start and grow over time, which is close but is about developing it, not about making it deeper.
The answer is option (4), enhance.

review.note: The key's digit for Q16 sits under the watermark; it reads 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++fascination++.

explanation: 'fascination' is the feeling of being strongly attracted to and amazed by something interesting.
Clue: 'each corner revealing a new surprise'. She was amazed by what she saw, which is 'wonder'.
'curiosity' is tempting, but it is the wish to find out; fascination is the amazed feeling when you do see it. 'delight' and 'ecstasy' are about happiness, not amazement.
The answer is option (2), wonder.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++illuminate++.

explanation: To 'illuminate' is to light something up.
The sunset lit up the sky 'with brilliant shades of orange and pink', so the closest word is 'brighten'.
'adorn' means to decorate. 'highlight' and 'accentuate' mean to make one part stand out, not to fill something with light.
The answer is option (2), brighten.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++frail++.

explanation: 'frail' means physically weak and delicate, often because of old age. The man is 'elderly'.
'feeble' also means very weak.
'weary' means tired, which passes after a rest. 'slender' means thin in an attractive way, and 'gentle' describes how a person behaves.
The answer is option (1), feeble.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++enlighten++.

explanation: To 'enlighten' someone is to give them knowledge and understanding.
Clue: the stories would enlighten her 'in ways books never could'. Books teach us, so the comparison is about learning: 'educate'.
'inspire' is tempting because the stories are 'inspirational', but inspire and motivate mean to make someone want to do something, not to give understanding.
The answer is option (2), educate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the launch?
options: Reservations for the shoes can be made online.
Only a limited number of shoes will be available.
Anyone can purchase the shoes on 12 December.
Falcon shoes will be sold at all Sports House outlets.

explanation: Check each statement against the poster (Text 1).
The poster says 'Only 100 pairs!' A fixed, small number means the supply is limited, so statement (2) is true.
(1) is false: 'No reservations for customers or online purchases.' (3) is false: the launch is 'Exclusively for Sports House members'. (4) is false: it is only 'at the Vista City Outlet'.
The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: What kind of poster is shown in Text 1?

explanation: Ask: what does the poster want the reader to do?
It announces a 'sales launch', gives a price ($129.90), has a catchy slogan ('DON'T RUN, FLY!') and lists the shoe's selling points. It wants people to come and buy the Falcon.
A poster that advertises a product so that people will buy it is promotional.
'informational' is tempting because the poster gives a date and place, but those details serve the main aim, which is to sell. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Linda often experiences pain in her feet and prefers to run at night. Based on the information in Text 1, which features of the shoes would be most important for her?

explanation: Linda has two needs. Match each one to a feature box on the poster.
She runs at night: D) Visibility, 'Reflective materials keep you visible in low light'. That leaves options (3) and (4).
She often has pain in her feet: F) Support, 'Provides stability for injury-free running'. E) Durability is only about how long the shoes last, which does not help with pain.
The answer is option (3), D and F.

review.note: The word 'feet' in the question has a pen stroke through it in the scan (a previous owner's mark); the printed word is 'feet'.

questions.stem: What is the **main message** of Text 2?
options: It is easy to choose a pair of running shoes.
Running shoes are for the young and old.
Proper running shoes makes one run faster.
Wearing the right pair of running shoes is important.

explanation: The main message is the idea the whole text supports. Look at the first and last paragraphs.

First sentence: 'Wearing the right shoes is important for every runner'. Conclusion: choosing the right pair 'is an important one'. The middle paragraphs give the reasons (support, cushioning, balance).
(3) is only a detail and is not even stated: the text says runners 'perform well' and run 'more efficiently', not simply faster. (1) is the opposite of the point that the decision matters.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Both the descriptions for the shoes in Text 1 and the content of Text 2 __________.
options: offer tips on how to select running shoes
compare different features of running shoes
highlight the importance of quality running shoes

explanation: The word 'Both' is the key: the answer must be true of Text 1's feature descriptions **and** of Text 2.

Text 1's boxes tell what good shoes do for a runner (comfort, grip, support, injury-free running). Text 2 explains that good shoes help runners perform well and prevent injuries. Both show why good-quality running shoes matter.
(1) fits only Text 1; Text 2 does not advertise any shoe. Neither text compares features with one another or gives step-by-step tips for choosing.
The answer is option (4).

review.note: The key's digit for Q25 sits under the watermark; it reads 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins two clauses: 'They occur' and 'the diaphragm ... suddenly contracts'. We need a connector.
The second clause tells us the time at which hiccups happen, so the connector is 'when'.
'although' and 'unless' are also connectors, but they show contrast and condition, which do not fit: hiccups happen at the moment the diaphragm contracts.
The answer is (P) when: 'They occur when the diaphragm ... suddenly contracts.'

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'a muscle under the lungs ___ helps you breathe' sits between commas and describes the diaphragm.
The blank must stand for 'a muscle' and be the subject of 'helps'. That is the job of a relative pronoun.
A muscle is a thing, so we use 'which' (for people we would use 'who').
The answer is (Q) which.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'breathe ___ air' needs a small word that completes the verb.
'breathe in' means to take air into the lungs. When the diaphragm contracts, air rushes into the body.
The answer is (D) in: 'makes you breathe in air very fast'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'causing ___ familiar "hic" sound' needs an article before the noun phrase.
Everyone knows this particular sound, and the word 'familiar' tells us it is a known, specific one. For something specific and known we use 'the'.
'an' is wrong because 'familiar' starts with a consonant sound.
The answer is (J) the.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'There are ___ reasons' needs a quantity word before a plural countable noun.
'many' goes with countable nouns (many reasons); 'much' goes with uncountable nouns (much air).
The next sentences list several reasons (eating too quickly, swallowing air, laughing, feeling nervous), which confirms 'many'.
The answer is (F) many.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'on ___ own' is a fixed phrase meaning 'by itself or themselves, without help'. The blank is a possessive word.
The word must match the noun it points back to: 'hiccups', which is plural. So we use 'their', not 'its'.
The answer is (K) their: 'hiccups ... stop on their own'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'get rid of' is a fixed phrase meaning to remove or be free from something.
The verb phrase always takes 'of': get rid of hiccups, get rid of rubbish.
The answer is (H) of.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank starts a sentence and comes before the plural noun 'methods'.
The methods were just listed in the sentence before (holding their breath, drinking water slowly, breathing into a paper bag). To point back to plural things just mentioned, use 'these'.
The answer is (L) these: 'These methods help the diaphragm relax'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'goes back ___ normal' needs a preposition that shows returning to a state.
We say 'go back to' or 'return to' something: back to school, back to normal.
The answer is (M) to.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins two clauses with opposite ideas: hiccups are 'harmless' (good) but 'they can be annoying' (not so good).
A connector of contrast is needed. 'although' means 'even though'.
'unless' means 'if not' and would make no sense here.
The answer is (A) although: 'Hiccups are harmless, although they can be annoying.'

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++occassion++.

explanation: This is a spelling error.
'occasion' has a double 'c' but only one 's': oc-ca-sion.
A way to remember: two c's, one s, like the word 'accuse'.
The correct word is 'occasion'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++appearence++.

explanation: This is a spelling error.
The noun comes from 'appear' + '-ance', not '-ence': appear-ance.
Words in the same family: appear, disappear, appearance, disappearance.
The correct word is 'appearance'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++embrassed++.

explanation: This is a spelling error: letters are missing.
'embarrassed' has a double 'r' and a double 's': em-bar-rass-ed.
The underlined word left out 'ar' in the middle.
The correct word is 'embarrassed'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++wore++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the helping verb in front: 'she **had** accidentally ___'.
Rule: had + past participle makes the past perfect tense. 'wore' is the simple past form, not the past participle.
wear, wore, worn: the past participle is 'worn'.
The correct word is 'worn'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++on++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
The fixed phrase is 'in a rush' or 'in her rush to do something'.
'in her frantic rush to leave home' means while she was hurrying to leave.
The correct word is 'in'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++soft++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong word class.
The word describes **how** everyone chuckled. A word that describes a verb is an adverb.
'soft' is an adjective (a soft pillow). Add -ly to make the adverb: softly.
The correct word is 'softly'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++comfort++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong word class.
The blank is in a list of describing words before the noun 'hug': 'a warm, ___ hug'. It must be an adjective, like 'warm'.
'comfort' is a noun or a verb. The adjective for something that gives comfort is 'comforting'.
The correct word is 'comforting'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++receives++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong tense.
The whole passage tells what happened 'Last Saturday', and the other verbs are in the past: gathered, arrived, gave.
'receives' is present tense. Change it to the simple past.
The correct word is 'received' (remember: i before e except after c).

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++elegeant++.

explanation: This is a spelling error: there is an extra letter.
'elegant' is spelt e-l-e-g-a-n-t. There is no 'e' after the 'g'.
Say it in three beats: el-e-gant.
The correct word is 'elegant'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++convinient++.

explanation: This is a spelling error.
'convenient' is spelt con-ve-ni-ent: 'e' after the 'v', then 'ni'.
The underlined word used 'i' instead of 'e' in the second syllable.
The correct word is 'convenient'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence says courtesy is shown ___ simple greetings. The greetings are the **way** or the means of showing courtesy.
The preposition that means 'by means of' is 'through'.
'with' and 'using' give the same meaning and also fit.
The answer is 'through'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'where ___ feels valued' needs a subject for the verb 'feels'.
'feels' is singular, and a positive, friendly environment is good for all the people in it. The singular pronoun that means all people is 'everyone'.
'all' would need the plural verb 'feel', so it does not fit.
The answer is 'everyone' ('everybody' means the same).

review.note: The printed number (47) under this blank is almost entirely missing from the scan; only a bracket is visible. It is the blank between (46) and (48).

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Rules are designed to ___ safety, fairness, and order for all.' After 'to' we need a base verb that says what rules do for safety.
Rules make sure that these things are there. 'ensure' means to make certain that something happens.
'maintain' (keep up) and 'promote' (encourage) also make sense with safety, fairness and order.
The answer is 'ensure'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the list: '___ patiently for one's turn, **keeping** noise levels low ... and **following** instructions'. All items in a list take the same form, so the blank is an -ing word.
What do we do patiently 'for one's turn'? We wait. The phrase is 'wait for one's turn'.
The answer is 'waiting'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'ways to demonstrate self-discipline and ___ for others' needs a noun that goes with 'for others'.
The paragraph begins 'Respecting school rules'. Waiting your turn and keeping quiet in the library show that you respect other people.
'consideration for others' has a similar meaning and also fits.
The answer is 'respect'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'how your actions ___ possibly affect other people' has the base verb 'affect' after the blank, so the blank is a modal (helping) verb.
The word 'possibly' shows that it is about possibility, not certainty. Modals of possibility are may, might, can and could.
The answer is 'may'. 'can', 'could' and 'might' fit in the same way.

review.note: Solved answer was 'can'; the key gives 'may'. Both are modals of possibility that fit 'possibly affect', so 'can', 'could' and 'might' are in the accept list.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'including quieter students in group ___' needs a noun that goes with 'group' and that students do together.

Quieter students tend to be left out when a group is talking, so the best fit is 'group discussions'. The verb after the blank is 'are', but its subject is the whole list (Helping ..., offering ..., or including ...), so the blank can be plural or uncountable.
'group activities', 'group work' and 'group projects' also make sense.
The answer is 'discussions'.

review.note: Solved answer was 'activities'; the key gives 'discussions'. Both collocate with 'group' and fit the sentence, so 'activities', 'work', 'projects' and 'tasks' are in the accept list.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'both ___ and shared resources': the word 'both ... and' pairs two kinds of resources, and one of them is 'shared'.
We need an adjective that contrasts with 'shared': things that belong to one person. That is 'personal'.
The next sentence gives examples of shared resources (borrowed books, the canteen, school property), which confirms the contrast.
The answer is 'personal'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'using school property ___ care' describes **how** the property is used.
The fixed phrase is 'with care', which means carefully: handle with care.
The answer is 'with'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'help to strengthen existing bonds ___ maintain good relationships' joins two base verbs that follow 'help to': strengthen and maintain.
Both are good results that happen together, so they are joined with 'and'.
The answer is 'and'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Handling disagreements ___ they arise' joins 'handling disagreements' to the clause 'they arise' (they come up).
The clause tells the time: we handle disagreements at the time they come up. The connector is 'when'.
'as they arise' and 'whenever they arise' mean the same.
The answer is 'when'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'when you are in ___ about a difficult concept' needs a noun that completes the phrase 'in ___ about'.
The fixed phrase is 'in doubt', which means not sure. You ask questions when you are not sure about something.
The answer is 'doubt'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the list after 'by': 'by **participating** in community activities, ___ kind towards newcomers, and **helping** others'. Every item is an -ing word.
The blank is followed by the adjective 'kind'. The verb that links to an adjective is 'be': be kind.
Put 'be' into the -ing form to match the list: 'being kind towards newcomers'.
The answer is 'being'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'positive ___ such as graciousness and gratitude': the blank is a plural noun, and 'such as' gives two examples of it.
Graciousness and gratitude are good qualities that guide how we behave. Such qualities are called 'values'.
'qualities', 'traits' and 'attitudes' also describe them.
The answer is 'values'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'students ___ to a better school experience' needs a verb that is followed by 'to' and agrees with the plural subject 'students'.
'contribute to' means to help to bring something about. Students who show good values help to make school better for everyone.
The answer is 'contribute'.

questions.stem:
I was impressed by how deep her knowledge was.
____________________ of her knowledge.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: I was impressed by the depth of her knowledge.

explanation: The ending 'of her knowledge' needs a noun in front of it: the ___ of her knowledge.
Change the adjective 'deep' into its noun form: deep becomes 'depth' (like wide, width and long, length).
'how deep her knowledge was' becomes 'the depth of her knowledge'. Drop 'how' and 'was'.
Answer: I was impressed by the depth of her knowledge. Spell 'depth' correctly and keep 'was impressed' in the past tense.

review.keyAnswer: I was impressed by the depth of her knowledge.
review.solvedAnswer: I was impressed by the depth of her knowledge.

questions.stem:
We left immediately when the movie ended.
As soon as ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: As soon as the movie ended, we left.
accept: As soon as the movie ended we left

explanation: 'As soon as' means 'immediately when', so it replaces both words. Do not write 'immediately' again.
The event that happened first follows 'As soon as': the movie ended. Then comes what happened next: we left.
Keep both verbs in the simple past: ended, left.
Answer: As soon as the movie ended, we left.

review.keyAnswer: As soon as the movie ended, we left.
review.solvedAnswer: As soon as the movie ended, we left.

questions.stem:
David does not like to play computer games. He likes to read.
____________________ would rather ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: David would rather read than play computer games.

explanation: 'would rather A than B' shows preference: the thing the person likes comes first, the thing he does not like comes after 'than'.
Rule: after 'would rather' and after 'than', use the base form of the verb with no 'to': read, play.
David likes reading, so 'read' goes first; 'play computer games' goes after 'than'.
Answer: David would rather read than play computer games.

review.keyAnswer: David would rather read than play computer games.
review.solvedAnswer: David would rather read than play computer games.

questions.stem:
"Did you sit for the Science test last week?" Mother asked Sarah.
Mother asked Sarah ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Mother asked Sarah if she had sat for the Science test the previous week.
accept: Mother asked Sarah whether she had sat for the Science test the previous week.
Mother asked Sarah if she had sat for the Science test the week before.
Mother asked Sarah whether she had sat for the Science test the week before.

explanation: This is a yes/no question in reported speech. Join it with 'if' or 'whether', and use statement word order (subject before verb) with no question mark.
Pronoun: 'you' is Sarah, so it becomes 'she'.
Tense moves one step back: 'Did you sit' (simple past) becomes 'had sat' (past perfect).
Time word: 'last week' becomes 'the previous week' or 'the week before'.
Answer: Mother asked Sarah if she had sat for the Science test the previous week.

review.keyAnswer: Mother asked Sarah if she had sat for the Science test the previous week.
review.solvedAnswer: Mother asked Sarah if she had sat for the Science test the previous week.

questions.stem:
She is such a nice person. She collected my worksheets for me when I was absent.
It was so ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: It was so nice of her to collect my worksheets for me when I was absent.
accept: It was so nice of her to have collected my worksheets for me when I was absent.

explanation: The pattern is: It was + so + adjective + of + person + to-infinitive. It praises a person for something he or she did.
'such a nice person' becomes 'so nice'. After 'of', the pronoun changes to the object form: 'she' becomes 'her'.
The action follows as a to-infinitive: 'collected' becomes 'to collect'.
Answer: It was so nice of her to collect my worksheets for me when I was absent.

review.keyAnswer: It was so nice of her to collect my worksheets for me when I was absent.
review.solvedAnswer: It was so nice of her to collect my worksheets for me when I was absent.

questions.stem: From paragraph 1, state three **physical** signs that tell us how terribly parched Brian had been.

parts.label: a

answer.value: Brian's mouth was dry and tasted foul and sticky.

explanation: 'parched' means extremely thirsty and dried out. A **physical** sign is something that can be seen or felt on his body.
Paragraph 1, third sentence: 'His mouth was dry and tasted foul and sticky.'
The marker looks for the mouth being dry (and tasting foul and sticky). 'He was viciously thirsty' is a feeling, not a physical sign, so it does not score.

parts.label: b

answer.value: His lips were cracked and seemed as if they were bleeding.

explanation: Paragraph 1, fourth sentence: 'His lips were cracked and seemed as if they were bleeding.'
Cracked lips are a sign of a body that has dried out.
The marker looks for: lips cracked (and seemed to be bleeding).

parts.label: c

answer.value: His skin was all withered up.

explanation: Paragraph 1, fifth sentence: 'His skin was all withered up.' 'withered' means dried up and shrivelled, like a plant without water.
Do not give the burn on his face or the blistering: those are signs of sunburn, caused by the sun while he slept, not signs of thirst.
The marker looks for: skin all withered up. The three signs may be written in any order.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Brian's mouth was dry and tasted foul and sticky. (b) His lips were cracked and seemed as if they were bleeding. (c) His skin was all withered up.
review.solvedAnswer: Mouth dry, foul and sticky; lips cracked and seeming to bleed; skin all withered up. Agrees with key.
review.note: A previous owner drew a line through 'all withered up' and under 'if they' in the scan; the printed words are transcribed.

questions.stem:
Brian struggled hard to decide if he wanted to try drinking water from the lake. Using information from lines 6 to 17 (paragraphs 2 and 3), complete the following tables.
[[table1]]
[[table2]]

header: Reason why Brian thought that way:

rows.t: (a) Brian thought he ++should drink++ water from the lake because

rows: (ii) his mouth and throat raged with thirst.
(iv) he had swallowed a lot of the water in the lake and was fine.

header: Reason why Brian thought that way:

rows.t: (b) Brian thought he ++should not drink++ water from the lake because

rows: (i) he felt the idea of drinking water from a lake was awful.
(iii) the water looked a little murky.

parts.label: ai
parts.prompt: Table (a), reason (i): Brian thought he ++should drink++ water from the lake because

answer.value: The lake was blue and looked clean.

explanation: Table (a) lists Brian's reasons **for** drinking. The reasons follow the order of the passage, and reason (ii), 'his mouth and throat raged with thirst', is given.
Read the words just before it in paragraph 2: 'but the lake was blue, looked clean and his mouth and throat raged with thirst'.
So reason (i) is that the lake was blue and looked clean.

parts.label: aiii
parts.prompt: Table (a), reason (iii): Brian thought he ++should drink++ water from the lake because

answer.value: There might not be another water source he could drink from.

explanation: Reason (iii) lies between (ii) 'raged with thirst' and (iv) 'he had swallowed a lot of the water'.
Between them is the question in Brian's mind: 'Would there be another water source he could drink from?'
Turn the question into a reason: he did not know if there was any other water source, so the lake might be his only water.

parts.label: bii
parts.prompt: Table (b), reason (ii): Brian thought he ++should not drink++ water from the lake because

answer.value: There were thick, prickly grasses in the way.

explanation: Table (b) lists the reasons **against** drinking. Reason (iii), 'the water looked a little murky', is given, and the reasons are in passage order.
Read the words just before it in paragraph 3: 'Along the edge, there were thick prickly grasses in the way and the water looked a little murky.'
So reason (ii) is the thick prickly grasses in the way, which made the water hard to get to.

parts.label: biv
parts.prompt: Table (b), reason (iv): Brian thought he ++should not drink++ water from the lake because

answer.value: There were small bugs swimming in the water.

explanation: Reason (iv) comes after 'the water looked a little murky'.
The next sentence: 'He scowled in disgust at the small bugs swimming in the water'. 'scowled in disgust' shows how much this put him off.
So reason (iv) is that there were small bugs swimming in the water.

review.keyAnswer: (a)(i) The lake was blue and looked clean. (a)(iii) There might not be another water source he could drink from. (b)(ii) There were thick, prickly grasses in the way. (b)(iv) There were small bugs swimming in the water.
review.solvedAnswer: (a)(i) the lake was blue and looked clean; (a)(iii) he did not know if there was another water source; (b)(ii) thick prickly grasses in the way; (b)(iv) small bugs swimming in the water. Agrees with key.
review.note: The paper prints [2m] beside each of the two tables, so Question 67 carries 4 marks (1 mark for each of the four blanks); this matches the page totals and the section total of 20. For (b)(ii), 'he did not know if he could drink it' (paragraph 2) was also considered, but it comes before reason (i) in the passage; the key's answer keeps the passage order.

questions.stem: Based on information from lines 12 to 17 (paragraph 3), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Brian had injured himself in the plane wreck.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Brian had a badly bruised forehead and an aching body.

explanation: Paragraph 3, first sentence: his situation consisted of 'a plane wreck, a badly bruised forehead, an aching body and a thirst'.
A badly bruised forehead and an aching body are injuries, and they are listed right after the plane wreck. So the statement is True.
The reason must be evidence from the passage (bruised forehead, aching body), not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Brian could not think too well because he was dehydrated.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. The thirst tore at Brian until he could not think.

explanation: 'dehydrated' means the body does not have enough water, which is why he was so thirsty.
Paragraph 3, first sentence: 'a thirst that tore at him until he could not think'. The thirst was so strong that it stopped him from thinking.
So the statement is True, and the reason is that his thirst tore at him until he could not think.

review.keyAnswer: (a) True --- Brian had a badly bruised forehead and an aching body. (b) True --- The thirst tore at Brian until he could not think.
review.solvedAnswer: (a) True: badly bruised forehead and aching body; (b) True: a thirst that tore at him until he could not think. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Which word from lines 18 to 23 (paragraph 4) tells us that Brian was moving unsteadily on the log?

explanation: The question asks for one word about **how he moved**, so look for a verb of movement in paragraph 4.
'He balanced on the log, holding himself up with the limbs, and **teetered** out past the weeds and muddy water.'

To 'teeter' is to move in an unsteady way, as if about to fall. 'balanced' is the trap: it means he kept steady, which is the opposite. ('staggered' also means unsteady, but it is in paragraph 5 and he was no longer on the log.)
The answer is 'teetered'. Copy one word only, spelt exactly.

questions.stem:
Brian spent quite some time at the log on the lake. Based on information from lines 18 to 28 (paragraphs 4 and 5), fill in the following table.
[[table1]]

rows: **How Brian felt about the water in the lake in (a)**
Brian thought he would just try a sip, still pondering over the lake water.
**How Brian felt about the water in the lake in (b)**
Brian felt that he was past caring whether or not the water in the lake was good and safe enough to drink.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How Brian felt about the water in the lake in (a)

answer.value: Brian felt undecided (unsure whether the water in the lake was good and safe enough to drink).

explanation: Look at what Brian thought: he 'would **just try a sip**, still **pondering** over the lake water'.
'pondering' means still thinking it over, and taking only a sip shows he was being careful. He had not made up his mind whether the water was safe.
The given answer for (b) helps: by then he 'was past caring whether or not the water ... was good and safe enough to drink'. So in (a) he still cared and was unsure.
The marker looks for a feeling such as undecided, unsure, doubtful or hesitant about the water.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Brian could not stop drinking the lake water (he stooped, put his mouth to the lake and drank and drank in great gulps) as he was too thirsty.

explanation: The feeling given for (b) is that he 'was past caring' whether the water was safe. Find the action that shows this.

End of paragraph 4: once the cold water touched his lips, 'he could not stop'. Paragraph 5: 'He stooped and put his mouth to the lake and drank and drank ... swallowing great gulps of it. He drank until his stomach was swollen'.
The marker looks for an action: he could not stop drinking, or he drank and drank great gulps of the lake water. Write what he **did**, not how he felt.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Brian felt undecided. (b) Brian could not stop drinking the lake water as he was too thirsty and hot.
review.solvedAnswer: (a) He was still unsure whether the water was safe to drink; (b) he put his mouth to the lake and drank and drank, unable to stop. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: When Brian 'felt the cold lake water trickle past his cracked lips and over his tongue, he could not stop' (lines 22–23, paragraph 4, from "mouth and felt" to "could not stop"). What was it he could not stop doing?

answer.value: Brian could not stop drinking the lake water.
accept: He could not stop drinking the lake water.
He could not stop drinking the water from the lake.
Drinking the water from the lake

explanation: The sentence does not say what he could not stop, so read on to see what he did next.
Paragraph 5: 'He stooped and put his mouth to the lake and **drank and drank**'. Before that, he had only meant to 'try a sip'.
So what he could not stop doing was drinking the water from the lake.
The marker looks for: drinking (the lake water).

review.keyAnswer: Brian could not stop drinking the lake water.
review.solvedAnswer: He could not stop drinking the lake water.

questions.stem: Why did Brian throw up most of the water he had drunk?

answer.value: Brian had drunk too much water, until his stomach was swollen, and he felt sick, so he threw up most of the water.

explanation: Find 'threw up' at the end of paragraph 5 and read the cause just before it.
'He drank until his stomach was swollen, until he nearly fell off the log with it ... he was immediately sick and threw up most of the water.' He had also been 'swallowing great gulps'.
He took in far more water than his stomach could hold, and that made him sick.
The marker looks for: he drank too much water (until his stomach was swollen).

review.keyAnswer: Brian had drunk too much water until his stomach was swollen and he felt sick, so he threw up most of the water.
review.solvedAnswer: He drank too much water too quickly, until his stomach was swollen. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a
explanation: A pronoun like 'It' points back to something just mentioned. Read the sentence before it.
'His face felt like it was on fire. **It** was going to blister and peel.' What was going to blister and peel after being burnt by the sun? His face.
Test by replacing the word: 'His face was going to blister and peel.' It makes sense.
The answer is Brian's face.

parts.label: b
explanation: 'He drank until his stomach was swollen, until he nearly fell off the log with **it**'.
What made him so heavy that he nearly fell off the log? The stomach that was swollen with water, mentioned just before.
Earlier in the paragraph, 'it' ('pulling it deep', 'great gulps of it') means the water, but this 'it' follows 'his stomach was swollen', so it points to the swollen stomach.
The answer is Brian's swollen stomach.

parts.label: c
explanation: 'He pulled himself once more up the bank to the tall tree without branches and sat again with his back against **it**.'
What did he lean his back against? The nearest noun that fits is the tall tree. ('the bank' does not fit: he climbed up the bank to reach the tree.)
Test by replacing the word: 'sat again with his back against the tall tree'. It makes sense.
The answer is the tall tree without branches.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Brian's face (b) Brian's swollen stomach (c) the tall tree without branches
review.solvedAnswer: (a) his face; (b) his swollen stomach; (c) the tall tree without branches. Agrees with key.
review.note: Part of the key for (b) and (c) is under the watermark but readable. The three pronouns asked about are bold in the passage, as printed.

questions.stem:
Write 1, 2 and 3 in the blanks below to indicate the order in which the events occurred in the story.
_____ Brian fell asleep under the sun.
_____ Brian's plane crashed.
_____ Brian drank water from the lake.
(Type the three numbers in the order of the blanks from top to bottom, for example 3, 2, 1.)

explanation: Be careful: the order in which the passage **tells** things is not the order in which they **happened**.
The plane crash came first. It is only mentioned later as something already over: he swallowed water 'while he was swimming out of the plane' and his situation included 'a plane wreck'.
Next he fell asleep: when the passage opens he has just woken up, and 'The sun had come over him and cooked him while he slept.'
Last, after waking, he walked down to the lake and drank (paragraphs 4 and 5).
So: Brian fell asleep under the sun is 2, Brian's plane crashed is 1, Brian drank water from the lake is 3. The answer is 2, 1, 3.

review.keyAnswer: Brian fell asleep under the sun — 2; Brian's plane crashed — 1; Brian drank water from the lake — 3.

questions.stem: Using information from lines 29 to 33 (paragraph 6), answer the following questions.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Which **ONE** of the following words best describes how Brian felt in the last paragraph about what was happening? Put a tick in the box beside your answer.

explanation: Look at how the last paragraph ends: 'but there were things he knew he had to do.'

Brian was feeling better (his thirst was gone and the pain in his head was less), and instead of just resting he was already thinking about what he must do next. A person who has made up his mind to act is 'determined'.
He was not 'disappointed' (things had improved) or 'puzzled' (he **knew** what he had to do). 'affirmed' means confirmed or declared to be true; it is not a feeling about what to do next.
The answer is 'determined'.
